diagnostic_hypotheses.H1-A-REPRESENTATION: A's pomaze failure is REPRESENTATION: the policy is state-blind by construction (neutral specialists ignore the observation; action depends only on learned gains). D1: corr(stimulus_c, beacon) ~ 0 for all channels (|r| < 0.10 on every seed) — measured, not assumed. D2: all channel gains decay to the 0.01 floor on canonical pomaze and stay there regardless of episode outcome. D3: DENSE does not lift A (dense_mean - std_mean <= 0.5) — shaping cannot be exploited without state input. D4: in NEAR, A's gains show no systematic response to goal hits and post-first-goal episodes do not improve (mean of post-goal eps - mean of pre-goal eps <= 0.2): the delta rule attributes +1.0 to whichever channel won the goal step — maze-seed-independent luck, not a learnable policy.
diagnostic_hypotheses.H2-B-EXPLORATION-plus-REPRESENTATION-BOU: B's pomaze failure is EXPLORATION-dominant with a linear-head REPRESENTATION bound. D5: P(goal in 15 canonical eps) < 0.20 on >= 5/6 seeds (no positive mean returns, matching the battery). D6: DENSE lifts B substantially (dense_mean - std_mean > 1.0): the near-linear beacon gradient IS learnable by the linear reward head, so the sparse failure is reward-findability, not inability to use reward. D7 (credit assignment registers): on goal trials in DENSE/NEAR, B's reward prediction moves — mean|1.0 - rhat_probe| on recorded goal-step (obs_vec, action) probes is smaller when re-evaluated at run end than at the time of the trial (second-half goal trials: |rerr| < first-half |rerr|). D8 (representation bound): on canonical pomaze n_contexts == 1 (no categorical obs fields; verified), so position must ride mu0 ~= obs vector; the 5-channel position signature (wall_n/s/e/w, beacon; 64 combos) aliases across the ~49 walkable cells — measured aliasing rate from RANDOM rollouts (fraction of obs-keys seen at >=2 positions where the BFS-optimal action disagrees) is substantial (> 0.30), bounding what the linear head can represent.
diagnostic_hypotheses.H3-C-HABITUATION-CREDIT-ASSIGNMENT: C's pomaze failure is the inherited NR-A-006 decay expressed as habituation: flat predictor outputs -> habituated bids -> gains decay -> tie-break degeneracy. D9: on canonical pomaze, C's rhat stimulus stream has near-zero within-episode variance (std of rhat across ticks < 0.05 on >= 5/6 seeds), gains sit at floor, and arbitration margin < 1e-9 on > 0.90 of ticks (tie-break proxy). D10: in NEAR, even with frequent goal hits, C's gains stay at floor and post-goal episodes don't improve (same 0.2 rule as D4) — sparse reward never survives habituation. D11: DENSE partially lifts C (dense_mean - std_mean > 1.0): non-flat stimuli un-habituate the bids and gains leave the floor — proving the failure is the sparse-reward habituation loop, not navigation depth.

failure_classes.CREDIT_ASSIGNMENT: rewards are found (P_goal_near > 0.50) but post-goal episodes do not improve (post - pre <= 0.2) AND the machinery shows no registration on goal trials (B: goal-step |rerr| does not decline; A/C: gains flat through goal episodes)
failure_classes.EXPLORATION: rewards are rarely found (P_goal_std < 0.20) but the machinery demonstrably registers and exploits them when they are made available (dense/near lift > 1.0; goal-trial machinery movement per D7)
failure_classes.REPRESENTATION: the policy cannot use the available information even when reward is dense (dense lift <= 0.5) OR the machinery is provably blind to the needed state (A: stimuli perpendicular to obs; B: high obs aliasing + goal-step rhat fails to approach 1.0 after >= 5 exposures, |1.0 - rhat_probe_end| > 0.5) OR the signal is structurally attenuated (C: habituation kills non-flat stimuli)
